ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Regimen de Fundaciones de Interes Privado) as amended by Ley 62 de 2021; Decreto Ejecutivo 2 de 1996 (implementing regulations); Ley 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (AML/CFT regime, establishing the Unidad de Analisis Financiero) as amended by Ley 70 de 2019, Ley 97 de 2021 and Decreto Ejecutivo 169 de 2016; Ley 18 de 2019 (mandatory beneficial owner reporting to the Registro Publico); Reglamento de la Ley 23 (Resolucion UAF 1-2020).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founder and legal counsel, authenticated before Panama Notary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons under Ley 23 de 2015 arts. 11-12 and UAF Resolucion 1-2020; automated screening against OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU consolidated sanctions list, and Panamanian national CFT circulars; all founders, council members, protector, beneficiaries, and beneficial owners above the 25% threshold must be screened pre-incorporation; results documented in an AML/CFT risk file maintained by the resident agent for not less than five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Publico de Panama - Portal de Servicios en Linea (Sede: Registro Publico, Seccion de Fundaciones de Interes Privado; online name search/certificate issuance at https://www.registropublico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The foundation name must be written in Spanish and must begin with the word 'Fundacion'; foreign-language names are admitted only when transliterated into Spanish phonetic characters and rendered in Latin script; names shall not be merely numerical, shall not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered foundation or company, and shall not misrepresent the legal nature of the entity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant or its registered agent files a written 'recurso de apelacion' before the Direccion General del Registro Publico within 10 working days from notification, invoking Ley 38 de 2000 (Procedimiento Administrativo General); the submission must include the original name-certificate rejection notice, a requested alternative name, and supporting arguments on distinctiveness and non-confusion; the Registro Publico must resolve within 30 working days; if denied, the applicant may pursue the 'recurso de reconsideracion' and thereafter judicial review before the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso-Administrativo de la Corte Suprema de Justicia.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole location for the actual manufacturing operations: the surgical suture assembly business requires a physical production facility registered with the Ministry of Health (MINSA) and conformity with WHO GMP/ISO 13485 standards; the Private Interest Foundation's statutory registered office with the resident agent in Panama may be a legal-address-only facility, but the operative manufacturing plant must maintain physical premises, personnel, equipment, and controlled-environment inventory in the Republic of Panama or at a regulated foreign plant recognized by MINSA.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 65% - for the manufacturing entity within the first 18 months of operation due to mandatory medical-device establishment inspection by MINSA Departamento de Dispositivos Medicos under Decreto Ejecutivo 398 de 2015; 15% - likelihood of an unannounced on-site verification visit to the PIF's statutory registered agent office in the same period, limited to document-presentation verifications and compliance spot-checks.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 (Private Interest Foundations), as amended; Executive Decree No. 63 of 26 July 1996 (Implementing Regulations); Public Registry Interpretive Rules (Acuerdo No. 18 of 2004), Titles I and II.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama) – Sistema Integrado de Registro (SIRCE), Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Carta Fundacional (Foundation Charter) embodied in Escritura Pública No. ___ del Protocolo de la Notaría ___; inscribed via Formulario Único de Registro (FUR).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Law 25 of 1995 requires every foundation to declare a patrimonio fundacional (initial endowment) sufficient to achieve its stated purpose; the standard professional minimum is USD 10,000. No escrow account or paid-up deposit is mandated at formation; the endowment is declared in the Foundation Charter and attested by the Resident Agent. Foundation assets are autonomous, are not liable for founder personal debts, and may be increased by later council resolution.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST FOUNDATION COUNCIL RESOLUTION NO. 001/2025 — RESOLVED: (1) The Foundation Charter and the USD 10,000 initial endowment are ratified; (2) the registered office is adopted at the address given by the Resident Agent in Panama; (3) the following officers are appointed: President, Treasurer, and Compliance Secretary, each empowered to act jointly for banking, tax, and licensing matters; (4) the officers are authorized to obtain the RUC, the municipal Aviso de Operación, the MINSA sanitary registration for sterile sutures, the MiAMBIENTE environmental registration, and the Fire Brigade safety certificate; (5) the Resident Agent and law firm may execute all necessary filings with the Public Registry and line ministries.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability Search and Notarization of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública de la Ciudad de Panamá (notary-in-charge) with name screening via SIRCE online platform.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed Panamanian attorney acting as Resident Agent. Perform three name searches in the Public Registry database to confirm that the proposed foundation name is available. Draft the Carta Fundacional in Spanish containing: exact foundation name, registered office, purpose (manufacture, assembly, and commercialization of absorbable polyglycolic acid braided surgical sutures with needles – ISIC 3250), endowment, Foundation Council members, beneficiary and protector provisions, amendment and termination rules. Execute the Charter before a Panamanian notary and record it as an escritura pública in the notarial protocol.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of founder passport (Apostille or Panamanian consular legalization)
Name availability search reports for three proposed names
Proposed registered office address and utility bill
Declared initial endowment statement and purpose description
Resident Agent acceptance letter with professional license endorsement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or the Public Registry flags the name or purpose, select an alternate approved name and execute a notarial addendum to the Charter before the same notary; re-run the SIRCE availability search and resubmit within the original application window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription of the Foundation Charter in the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – SIRCE electronic filing window, Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the notarial protocol (escritura pública) into SIRCE together with the official tariff payment receipt and the Resident Agent certificate. The Registry verifies compliance with Law 25 of 1995 and issues the Certificado de Inscripción after approval. The foundation acquires distinct legal personality exclusively upon inscription in the Registry; no publication in the official gazette is required for private interest foundations.
required_dossiers: Notarized Foundation Charter (escritura pública) in full text
SIRCE registration application (FUR) signed by the Resident Agent
Payment receipt for the official state filing tariff
Resident Agent's current professional license and registration certificate
Notarial protocol number and date certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a nota de reparo (written objection), the attorney must answer within the statutorily granted ten working days; any substantive defect is cured by executing a corrective notarial addendum and re-presenting it to the Registry for continued examination without loss of filing priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Taxpayer Registration (RUC) at the Dirección General de Ingresos
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas – Sede Electrónica and Registro Único de Contribuyentes office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Certificado de Inscripción, register the foundation as a taxpayer and obtain the RUC. Submit the charter, registry certificate, officers' resolution, and the registered-office proof. Declare the territorial taxation regime and assign the CIIU activity code 3250 (manufacture of medical surgical goods). The foundation is subject to Panamanian income tax at the standard rate solely on Panama-source income; foreign-source income and capital gains remain outside the territorial tax scope. Register authorized signatories for local invoices and, if required, for import activities.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Inscripción issued by the Public Registry
Notarized Foundation Charter and amending instruments
First Foundation Council Resolution appointing officers and signatories
Registered-office proof (lease, title, or notarized occupancy letter)
Passport copies of the Foundation Council members and the Resident Agent
RUC application form and bank signature card for the foundation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI requests clarification on the activity classification, resubmit the dossier with a technical memorandum linking ISIC 3250 to medical-device production and attach the MINSA sanitary-registration filing receipt, thereby confirming the operational reality and avoiding reclassification as a pure financial holding entity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Aviso de Operación Industrial and Zoning Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipio de Panamá – Tesorería Municipal / Dirección de Licencias y Aviso de Operación, and Dirección de Gestión Urbana for zoning.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Aviso de Operación application at the municipality where the manufacturing and assembly plant is physically located. Present the RUC, foundation registration certificate, lease or title over the industrial premises, a zoning opinion, and a floor plan showing assembly lines, sterilization area, and needle-grinding bays. Pay the municipal operating tax calculated on declared assets and annual projected revenue, and affix the issued Aviso de Operación poster at the plant entrance. This permit is renewable in January of each year.
required_dossiers: Municipal Aviso de Operación application form
RUC certificate and taxpayer registration extract
Foundation registration certificate from the Public Registry
Notarized lease or title deed of the industrial premises
Zoning certificate (uso de suelo) for light manufacturing
Plant floor plan and machinery inventory description
Fire inspection request receipt (forwarded to the Fire Brigade)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Municipality denies the Aviso due to zoning incompatibility, file a written appeal within five business days and simultaneously petition the Dirección de Gestión Urbana for a special land-use authorization (cambio de uso de suelo); alternatively, relocate the plant to a designated industrial polygon and re-file the application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: MINSA Sanitary Registration for Absorbable PGA Suture Needle Assembly
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) – Dirección Nacional de Farmacia y Drogas, Departamento de Dispositivos Médicos.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the medical-device registration dossier for absorbable polyglycolic acid braided sutures with attached surgical needles under Executive Decree No. 1352 of 2015. The technical file must demonstrate conformity with ISO 13485 quality management, ISO 11137 sterilization validation, ISO 10993 biocompatibility, and the applicable pharmacopoeial monograph for PGA sutures. MINSA evaluates the dossier, may order a Good Manufacturing Practice inspection of the plant, and upon approval issues the Registro Sanitario de Dispositivos Médicos linked to the foundation's RUC, permitting national commercialization and import of raw polymer feedstocks.
required_dossiers: Medical-device sanitary registration application form (MINSA/DNDF)
RUC certificate and municipal Aviso de Operación copy
ISO 13485 certificate and GMP certificate of the manufacturing facility
Technical dossier: PGA polymer characterization, braiding parameters, needle alloy and swage attachment, resorption profile
Sterilization validation report under ISO 11137 (EtO or gamma)
Biocompatibility test reports under ISO 10993 (cytotoxicity, sensitization, irritation)
Spanish-language labels, instructions for use, and outer carton mock-ups
Certificate of analysis of the reference commercial batch
Free-sale certificate or prior registration from a reference country (preferred)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MINSA issues technical observations, the applicant has thirty calendar days (extendible once by fifteen days) to correct the dossier. If the technical file remains incomplete, MINSA may schedule a GMP inspection of the plant; a denial may be cured by reapplying under a corrected dossier after completing the missing sterility or biocompatibility testing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Verificación del Desempeño Ambiental and the respective Regional Office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Classify the suture braiding and needle assembly operation under Category I (low environmental risk). Complete the Ficha de Registro Ambiental in the Ventanilla Única de Ambiente describing effluent sources, sterilization modality (in-house EtO or outsourced gamma), generation of polymer offcuts and needle waste, and the wastewater discharge plan. Pay the environmental registration fee and obtain the Resolución de Registro Ambiental with binding compliance conditions, including periodic self-monitoring submissions to MiAMBIENTE.
required_dossiers: Ficha de Registro Ambiental (environmental registration form)
RUC certificate and municipal Aviso de Operación
Site plan, plant layout, and exact coordinates
Process description for braiding, coating, needle swaging, and sterilization
Waste management plan for PGA offcuts, used needles, and EtO residues
Preliminary wastewater characterization aligned with national discharge limits
Written commitment to comply with monitoring schedules
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MiAMBIENTE reclassifies the project to Category II because of EtO utilization, the operator must file a Category II Environmental Impact Assessment (Estudio de Impacto Ambiental, EIA) and implement expanded monitoring; the applicant may also return to Category I by contracting outsourced gamma sterilization, thereby eliminating in-situ EtO storage and emissions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Fire Brigade Safety Certificate and MITRADEL Occupational Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá – Departamento de Prevención y Seguridad; Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL) – Dirección de Higiene Ocupacional.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the fire-safety certificate by filing architectural plans, fire-load calculations, extinguishing system layouts, and the emergency evacuation plan; the Fire Brigade performs an on-site inspection and issues the corresponding R1/R2 certificate. Concurrently file the occupational hygiene clearance with MITRADEL: submit the workplace risk assessment, chemical-agent exposure monitoring plan (EtO and formaldehyde), personal protective equipment program, and annual medical surveillance report for employees handling sharps and sterile products.
required_dossiers: Fire certificate application with signed architectural floor plans
Fire-load calculation and emergency evacuation plan
Fire extinguisher and sprinkler system certification certificates
MITRADEL workplace registration form (Registro de Empresas)
Occupational risk assessment matrix for assembly lines and sterilization chambers
EtO and fine-particulate air monitoring results or validation plan
Personal protective equipment and employee medical surveillance programs
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Fire Brigade identifies structural deficiencies, complete the corrective construction works and request a reinspection within the granted ten-business-day extension. For MITRADEL, adopt a written compliance plan (plan de cumplimiento) with capped deadlines; any activity suspension is lifted once the occupational controls are verified by a follow-up inspection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Dirección General de Industrias (industrial registry and tariff classification) and Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) – Dirección Nacional de Farmacia y Drogas (medical-device sanitary control).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación Industrial (Municipio de Panamá) and Registro Sanitario de Dispositivos Médicos for absorbable polyglycolic acid braided sutures with needles (MINSA, Executive Decree No. 1352 of 2015).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Verificación del Desempeño Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I – Low Impact: Environmental Registration (Ficha / Registro Ambiental), not a full EIA study; mandatory before the start of operations and renewable every two years; reclassification to Category II applies only if in-house EtO sterilization and hazardous-waste storage thresholds are exceeded.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: pH 6.5–8.5; BOD5 ≤ 50 mg/L; COD ≤ 250 mg/L; TSS ≤ 50 mg/L; oil and grease ≤ 10 mg/L; zero detectable sterilant residues (EtO) in final effluent. Air: VOCs ≤ 50 mg/Nm3; PM10 ≤ 150 µg/m3; EtO workplace concentration below 1 ppm TWA. Solid medical waste (needle sharps, polymer offcuts, EtO residues) must be segregated in puncture-proof red containers and transferred to licensed hazardous-waste operators under Ley No. 1 de 1994 and Basel Convention transboundary rules.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá fire-safety certificate (R1/R2) covering structural fire load, sprinklers, and evacuation; municipal structural and zoning clearance for the industrial premises; and MITRADEL occupational hygiene approval under Resolución No. 102-2011, including EtO/formaldehyde air monitoring, machine-guarding inspection, personal protective equipment, and annual employee medical surveillance for needle-stick and sterilant exposure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá fire-safety certificate (R1/R2) covering structural fire load, sprinklers, and evacuation; municipal structural and zoning clearance for the industrial premises; and MITRADEL occupational hygiene approval under Resolución No. 102-2011, including EtO/formaldehyde air monitoring, machine-guarding inspection, personal protective equipment, and annual employee medical surveillance for needle-stick and sterilant exposure.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Republic of Panama; official taxpayer e-filing portal 'Sede Electrónica de la DGI' (e-Tax 2.0) at https://sede.dgi.gob.pa; export and customs controls administered by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) through the SICE single-window platform.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the Private Interest Foundation (PIF) under Panama Law 25 of 1995 before a Panamanian notary and Registered Agent, and register the Foundation Charter in the Registro Público de Panamá. Step 2: If the PIF will conduct domestic commercial, industrial, or export manufacturing activity (ISIC 3250), obtain an 'Aviso de Operación' (business notice) from the Ministry of Commerce and Industries (MICI) describing the exact surgical consumables manufacturing activity. Step 3: File the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) application with the DGI either at local revenue offices or through the Sede Electrónica, submitting: certified copy of the Foundation Charter, public registry certificate (personería jurídica), notarized registered-agent appointment, MICI Aviso de Operación, and evidence of the local bank account. Step 4: The DGI assigns the statutory 12-digit RUC and activates the taxpayer for Income Tax, Advance Tax (pago directo), and ITBMS obligations. Step 5: Complete the electronic invoicing habilitation under DGI Resolution No. 201-5420 of 2020, including issuance of digital signature certificates and DGI invoice folio authorization. A foreign entity without a Panamanian commercial presence must still obtain a non-resident RUC before deriving any Panama-source taxable income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not operate a US-style check-the-box election and has no hybrid-mismatch election. The statutory elections available to the PIF and its local export manufacturing operation include: (i) election of the Multinational Company Headquarters (SEM) regime under Law 41 of 2007 for qualifying regional services, attracting preferential payroll tax treatment and a 0% income tax rate on qualifying SEM revenues; (ii) election of the Maquila Regime under Law 12 of 1995 for manufacturing, assembly, and export operations, granting exemption from ITBMS and customs import duties; (iii) election to operate as a licensed free-zone enterprise (e.g., Panama Pacifico, Ciudad del Saber, Colon Free Trade Zone) under Law 32 of 2011; (iv) election of the simplified small-taxpayer regime (Régimen de Tributación Simplificada) where annual gross revenue does not exceed B/.36,000; (v) elective advance pricing agreements (APAs) for transfer pricing certainty under Law 41 of 2007; and (vi) the elective possibility of consolidating Panamanian group income where the local operating subsidiary is wholly owned by the foundation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS) — Panamanian VAT-type transfer tax on the supply of movable goods and provision of services, regulated by Articles 761-A et seq. of the Código Fiscal.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory ITBMS registration applies to any person habitually transferring taxable movable goods or rendering taxable services in Panama, without a general registration turnover threshold. The statutory small-taxpayer simplification ceiling is B/.36,000 (PAB, pegged 1:1 to USD) of annual gross revenue; a person with annual taxable turnover exceeding B/.36,000 must register, charge 7% ITBMS, and file monthly or quarterly declarations. Export-only producers may register voluntarily to support zero-rating of exports and recovery of input ITBMS credits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing under DGI Resolution No. 201-5420 of 4 December 2020, phased in by taxpayer RUC ranges. The local manufacturing entity must issue electronic invoices, electronic credit/debit notes, and transmission slips using the DGI-approved XML schema. The system requires: (i) prior DGI 'habilitación' and authorization of invoice folio numbering; (ii) use of a DGI-registered digital signature (Firma Electrónica); (iii) near-real-time transmission and automated validation by the DGI Sede Electrónica with an acknowledged receipt (acuse de recibo) before the document becomes fiscally valid; and (iv) retention of all fiscal tax records for at least 5 years. Panama does not operate a physical fiscal-stamp or prepaid clearance mechanism in the style of Mexico or Colombia, but the DGI performs immediate automated validation and may suspend invoice numbering upon detected non-compliance; customs export-related documents are separately cleared through the ANA SICE single window.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods and services rendered for use outside Panama are zero-rated (0% ITBMS) under the Código Fiscal, provided the supplier is a registered ITBMS taxpayer and the goods are physically shipped out of Panamanian territory. The PIF's surgical suture assembly operation qualifies when: (i) the buyer is a non-resident; (ii) legal title and physical risk pass outside Panama; (iii) shipment is supported by an ANA customs export declaration; and (iv) export proceeds are credited to the taxpayer's Panamanian bank account within the statutory term. Manufacturing-for-export under the Maquila Regime (Law 12 of 1995) or within a licensed free zone is simultaneously exempt from ITBMS and customs import duties on inputs such as polyglycolic acid raw material, needles, packaging, and assembly consumables. Excess ITBMS input credits generated by zero-rated exports are available for offset against domestic output tax or refundable through the DGI fiscal-credit mechanism.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación – DUE/DUM) filed electronically with the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) through the SICE single window
Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill for air cargo) evidencing export shipment from Panama to the foreign buyer

Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Ingreso de Divisas / SWIFT bank credit advice) proving receipt of export proceeds in Panama for ITBMS zero-rating and territorial income tax substantiation
Commercial export invoice and packing list fully matching the customs declaration, including ISIC 3250 product descriptions and batch numbers
Certificate of origin and technical/regulatory file for the surgical suture products if required by the destination medical-device regulator
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI may audit export zero-rating claims within a general assessment prescription of 5 years, extended to 7 years in cases of omission, false declarations, or fraud. An invalid or fraudulent zero-rating claim triggers: (i) retrospective clawback of the uncollected 7% ITBMS; (ii) moratory interest at 10% per annum on the underpaid tax; (iii) administrative fines generally ranging between 50% and 200% of the evaded tax depending on gravity and recidivism, plus fines for irregular invoicing; (iv) customs penalties and forfeiture or suspension of maquila/free-zone tax benefits; and (v) criminal liability for customs and tax fraud, including imprisonment for directors, officers, or the foundation's authorized agent where false export declarations have been certified, in accordance with the Código Fiscal, Ley 70 de 2019, and the Código Penal. The exporting taxpayer carries the burden of proof, including physical traceability of exported goods, shipping and insurance documentation, and SWIFT receipts, across the full retention and prescription horizon.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) as bank regulator; Banco Nacional de Panamá (BNP) serves as fiscal agent of the Republic of Panama. There is no traditional issuing or monetary-policy Central Bank. The National Treasury and the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) execute fiscal functions within a fully dollarized monetary framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is a fully dollarized economy: the Panamanian Balboa (PAB) exists only as a nominal accounting unit pegged 1:1 to the USD, with no separate paper currency. All capital account and current account transactions are freely convertible and there are no exchange controls or restrictions on profit remittance, dividend distribution, or principal repatriation for companies or Private Interest Foundations (PIFs). Remittances may be effected in USD without SBP authorization or special documentary filing, provided the underlying transactions comply with anti-money-laundering (AML) reporting thresholds and bank internal policies. Repatriation hurdles are effectively nil for lawful funds; the only practical constraint is satisfying bank KYC due diligence to prove lawful source and traceability of funds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio applies to export proceeds in Panama. Exporters, including manufacturers of surgical sutures under ISIC 3250, are permitted to retain 100% of export receipts in USD or any freely convertible currency in their designated Panamanian banking accounts. There is no requirement to surrender foreign currency to any central bank or public authority, and no obligation to declare settlement of export collections beyond standard SBP financial reporting executed by the commercial bank.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium. Panamanian law does not recognize offshore digital EMI (Electronic Money Institution) licenses as a substitute for a banking license issued by the SBP. A foreign fintech or EMI may not engage in deposit-taking, payment account issuance, or USD clearing settlement without obtaining either a General Banking License or a specific license under the SBP fintech regulatory sandbox. Offshore EMIs are legally constrained to operating through a licensed Panamanian bank as their settlement agent; this limits their viability as an autonomous treasury clearing rail. Their practical utility is confined to front-end payment APIs supported by an underlying SBP-regulated bank, with increased AML/KYC friction and no guarantee of acceptance by local clearing institutions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Most tier-1 Panamanian banks require physical presence for at least one director or foundation council member who will act as a signatory on the account. Remote onboarding is possible only where the bank already holds a strong pre-existing relationship, or when the signatory is a known corporate manager subject to a completed video interview and notarization through a Panamanian consulate. The Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) of the PA_PIF Private Interest Foundation is generally required to appear in person or to provide an independent professional validation (e.g., a compliance certification from a correspondent bank in an FATF-compliant jurisdiction). Non-resident directors may be accepted with apostilled corporate documents, police records, professional references, and an in-country executive manager appointed as a compliance-contact for the foundation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Private Interest Foundation (PIF) identified as an opaque offshore structure with non-transparent beneficial ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Foundation Charter and Regulations (Estatuto y Reglamento) registered in the Public Registry of Panama; authenticated register of Foundation Council members and Protector, if any; sworn declaration of UBO and signatories; notarized source of wealth letter; audited financial statements of the PIF; certificate of good standing and legal existence issued by the Public Registry; professional introduction from a reputable licensed lawyer or accountant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commercial activity in medical devices flagged for regulatory licensing and enhanced monitoring
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Panama Ministry of Health (MINSA) sanitary registration or medical device importation/manufacturing license; DIGEMI (Dirección General de Medicamentos e Insumos Médicos) certificate for absorbable sutures; facility inspection reports and Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) certification; commercial contracts and purchase orders from authorized surgical distributors; evidence of physical manufacturing site and inventory records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, or adverse-media hit on foundation members or trade counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Global sanctions screening report (OFAC, EU, UN) dated within 30 days; negative media and PEP assessment for each director, council member, and UBO; explanations and documentary support for any aging hits; export licenses, bills of lading, and marine/air cargo insurance evidencing genuine trade transactions; end-user certificates for surgical consumables routed to legitimate regional hospitals or distributors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value initial capital injection considered disproportionate to the stated manufacturing scope
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Contribution agreement and capital injection resolutions of the PIF; bank statements demonstrating lawful accumulation of funds in an established bank; commercial and financial projections for the ISIC 3250 suture assembly line; notarized purchase agreements for manufacturing equipment; certificate of registration of the PIF’s initial capital with the Public Registry.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Funds shall be routed via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 message types (depending on intermediary usage), with the payment referencing 'Capital Contribution to Private Interest Foundation PA_PIF, Grantor-Foundation Agreement dated XXXX, Public Registry Folio No. XXX'. Since Panama imposes no exchange controls, no central bank formality is required for the receipt of USD; however, the receiving commercial bank will require: (a) the sending bank’s KYC confirmation of the remitter; (b) the foundation charter and capital resolution approving the injection; (c) a statement of intended use for the capital (purchase of suture-needle assembly machinery, raw material procurement, payroll); (d) evidence of the lawful source of funds supported by prior account statements; and (e) for payments from US banks, a compliant OFAC-filtered instruction and the applicable SWIFT purpose code. In practice, the primary clearing channels are: direct USD transfers through Panamanian banks with U.S. correspondent accounts (Citibank, JPMorgan, BNY Mellon), or via the domestic Panama ACH/RTGS system for same-day local USD credit.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement for surgical suture raw materials and machinery will be executed using: (1) SWIFT MT103 for direct telegraphic transfers (T/T) to pay suppliers in the United States, Europe, and Asia; (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700, MT707 amendments) issued by Banistmo, Banco General, or Multibank against presentation of commercial invoice, bill of lading, packing list, insurance certificate, and MINSA sanitary authorization; (3) MT202COV for correspondent-driven corporate-to-corporate payments where intermediary bank routing requires formal cover instructions; and (4) domestic clearing through the Panama ACH (Cámara de Compensación de Panamá) for local payments to customs brokers, freight forwarders, and professional service providers. All outbound disbursements will be pre-matched to underlying trade agreements to maintain traceability for banking compliance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot FX contracts for conversion of USD into EUR, CNY, JPY, or GBP through Banco General, Banistmo, Multibank, or their correspondent trading desks
Outright FX forwards (up to 12 months) with licensed Panamanian banks for pre-payment of imported suture-needle equipment and PGA polymer raw materials

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for Latin American restricted currencies (e.g., Argentina Peso, Venezuelan Bolívar, and certain Andean currencies) executed through Miami-based trading desks or offshore banking units to hedge receivables from regional hospitals
Cross-currency swaps (USD/EUR, USD/CNY, USD/JPY) with international investment banks for long-term project financing or large equipment supply contracts
Optional FX options are permitted but not recommended at Stage 4; they are subject to board-approved hedging policy and SBP prudential scrutiny on a case-by-case basis

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Franchise Tax (Tasa Única Anual de Fundación de Interés Privado)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, Republic of Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 01 January through 31 March; payment must be received on or before 31 March; no anniversary-based extension
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment after 31 March increases the fee to USD 350 plus a 10% surcharge and monthly interest under the Panama Tax Code; no Paz y Salvo (good standing certificate) is issuable while unpaid; two consecutive unpaid years place the PIF on the Registry of Foundations default list and trigger administrative strike-off with asset forfeiture to the State.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation (Confirmación Anual de Beneficiarios Finales) endorsed by the registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Unified Beneficial Ownership Registry, submitted through the licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March each year, bundled with the franchise-tax payment; any membership or economic-interest change must be re-filed within 15 business days of the occurrence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omission prevents issuance of certificates of incumbency and good standing; penalties of up to USD 10,000 under Law 52 of 2016 against the foundation or its Council; repeated default may lead to mandatory deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts and Asset Inventory Record (Estados Financieros / Inventario de Activos) placed with the resident agent and the Foundation domicile
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered agent and, if appointed, the Foundation Protector — contractually required internal record, not filed with the public registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Certified as at 31 December of the prior year; must be physically or electronically available within 30 days of any demand by the Registro Público, DGI, or AML authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-availability within 30 days constitutes a breach of Law 52 of 2016 record-keeping duties; Foundation Council members become personally liable; the foundation may be treated as non-operative and administratively struck off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal Operating License Renewal (Renovación del Aviso de Operación; fee varies by declared gross receipts, USD 250 is the indicative small-scale minimum)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipio (Alcaldía) of the plant district, filed through the Ventanilla Única de Inversiones (Single Window)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between 01 and 31 January in the Panama district; other districts follow local ordinance dates; a newly established plant must register within 30 days of commencement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly surcharge of 10% on unpaid municipal tax; fines up to USD 1,000; temporary closure order for unlicensed operation; not applicable to an offshore-only PIF maintaining no physical plant in Panama.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Private Interest Foundation is not subject to statutory audit merely by its status under Law 25 of 1995. A mandatory independent audit arises only where (i) the Foundation Charter (Reglamento) expressly requires an external audit, or (ii) the foundation conducts Panamanian-source commercial or industrial operations and its gross annual revenue or total assets exceed the DGI threshold of USD 3,000,000, requiring audited financial statements by a licensed Panamanian CPA. A surgical-suture assembly operation located outside Panama remains outside the territorial tax net and does not trigger a Panamanian statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as endorsed by the Colegio de Contadores Públicos Autorizados de Panamá; IFRS for SMEs is acceptable for entities below the public-interest threshold; Law 52 of 2016 administrative record-keeping standards apply to all PIFs.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 52 of 2016 and its implementing Executive Decree, the PIF must lodge its natural-person beneficial-ownership schedule (25% or greater ownership or control, with a senior-management fallback) with the registered agent within 15 business days of formation and re-confirm it annually no later than 31 March. Any substitution of the economic interest or beneficiary must be re-filed within 15 business days. The registered agent retains certified KYC copies and updates the Registro Público electronic UBO database; the annual UBO confirmation is a precondition to issuing incumbency and good-standing certificates.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Registro de Miembros) per Law 25 of 1995
Register of the Foundation Council and Protector (Registro del Consejo y Protector de la Fundación)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 275 – USD 750 for a standard fiduciary arrangement; USD 750 – USD 1,500 for an active manufacturing PIF requiring enhanced UBO and AML administration
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required for an offshore-only PIF; voluntary review engagement USD 1,200 – USD 3,000; compulsory full IFRS audit USD 3,500 – USD 8,000 if Panama-source commercial activity triggers the mandate

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Panama's territorial system exempts foreign-source income: export proceeds and offshore manufacturing margins are not Panama-source unless booked through a Panamanian permanent establishment. Standard domestic ISIC 3250 manufacturers receive no general CIT holiday, but qualifying companies in the Colón Free Zone or Panama Pacifico benefit from a 5% preferential ISR regime; domestic producers may also claim duty and ITBMS exemptions on imported medical-grade raw materials, accelerated depreciation of assembly equipment, and the 5-year NOL carryforward.
